A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SARD research and contain readable main text and Appendices A–E. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, proofs, algorithm, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments comparing SARD with baselines on CIFAR-100, California Housing, and Pascal VOC in Section 6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original classification, regression, and object-detection experiments, including clean and adversarial results in Section 6 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The attack procedures, adversarial surrogate losses, regularized SARD objective, and Appendix C algorithm are unchanged. Newly cited top-k deferral methods are related work, not additions to SARD.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100 classification, California Housing regression, and Pascal VOC object detection under the same clean, untargeted, and targeted attack scenarios. Newly cited QA and top-k work does not expand evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Mao et al. (2023a), Mao et al. (2024c), and the Montreuil multi-task method. The latter changes citation from Montreuil et al. (2024) to Montreuil et al. (2025c), with the same procedure and results in Tables 3 and 9.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain the same splits, expert specializations, architectures, training budgets, accuracy/RMSE/mAP metrics, and PGD settings. Changes to optimizer and attack citation years do not indicate protocol changes.

E4.justification: The existing untargeted and agent-targeted robustness comparisons, including weak-expert scenarios and appendix model-targeted results, are retained. No ablation, sensitivity analysis, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions state in Appendix E that experiments report means and standard deviations over four independent trials. The uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–9 and the accompanying findings are unchanged. For example, untargeted CIFAR-100 accuracy remains 49.8 for SARD versus 17.2 for the baseline, and untargeted Pascal VOC mAP remains 39.0 versus 9.7.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, consistency bounds, computational-cost proposition, and Appendix D proofs are retained. Added consistency references do not alter the paper's formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about two adversarial attacks, SARD, consistency guarantees, and robustness across classification, regression, and multi-task learning.

C2.justification: The interpretations of rejector-only attacks, weak-expert vulnerability, clean-versus-adversarial performance, and SARD's applicability remain unchanged. The qualification added to earlier research is a positioning edit; no new limitation of SARD is stated.

D1.justification: Appendices C and E retain the same pseudocode, hyperparameters, hardware disclosure, checkpoint selection, and statement that scripts are publicly available. Neither version supplies a script-access link.

R1.justification: Sections 1–3 add references covering QA deferral, top-k deferral, and recent consistency research. Section 2 adds Montreuil et al. (2025a) on top-k experts and changes the account of prior realizable consistency from 'resolved' to 'tackled ... under specific conditions.' The central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: There are limited prose edits in related work, expanded citation groups, and extensive bibliographic metadata updates, including removal of direct reference URLs. The main narrative, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Longer citations and the expanded bibliography cause text reflow and shift appendix pagination. Updated baseline labels slightly change spacing in Tables 3 and 9. All three illustrations and nine tables retain their designs and substantive content.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves research context by acknowledging top-k deferral and qualifying earlier realizable-consistency results in Section 2. These limited contextual gains outweigh the reduced navigation convenience from removing bibliography URLs. The method, proofs, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
